anti_overlap: fd-statistical-calibration-procedure covers whether the picked value is statistically correct — this agent covers whether the correct value is correctly recorded and verifiable from the artifacts.
fd-null-baseline-semantic-validity covers whether the right agent was used — this agent covers whether the agent used matches what is recorded in the protocol and tarball.
fd-cli-arg-plumbing-correctness covers whether the flag reaches the sim — this agent covers whether the results of running the sim are correctly archived and cited in the protocol document.
decision_lens: Prioritizes findings where PROTOCOL.md §7a is updated with a value but the corresponding tarball artifacts (traces, analyzer output) are absent or inconsistent with that value, which would allow a replicator to re-run the calibration and get a different result. Secondary priority is the interaction between the attention-budget lock and other PENDING items in §12 that depend on it.
focus: Whether the attention-budget calibration result is correctly recorded in PROTOCOL.md §7a and §12, whether the calibration tarball is published in a form that satisfies the §11 reproducibility commitment, and whether locking this value creates any scope-amendment obligations under §9
name: fd-protocol-lock-integrity
persona: Apply the perspective of a pre-registration integrity auditor who reviews clinical trial protocol amendments — they care about whether the protocol document accurately reflects the procedure that was actually run, measure the gap between the 'pending' placeholder and the locked value, and flag any case where the lock-transition is incomplete, retroactively altered, or inconsistent with the artifacts in the tarball.
review_areas: §7a and §12 simultaneous update: the brainstorm specifies both §7a ('Value: [PENDING...]') and §12 (the attention-budget line in the DRAFT→LOCKED checklist) must be updated; verify that both sections are updated atomically in a single commit with the tarball artifacts, so there is no intermediate state where §7a is locked but §12 still lists it as pending.

Tarball artifact completeness: the brainstorm lists five deliverables including traces at B=5, B=10, B=20, a Python analyzer output, and the script running green; verify that all five are committed under docs/design/calibration/attention-budget/ and that the tarball's directory structure matches what the calibration script actually produces (trace subdirectories named b5/, b10/, b20/).

Protocol version consistency: PROTOCOL.md header says 'version: 0.1-draft' and 'status: DRAFT'; the attention-budget lock is a prerequisite for transitioning to LOCKED but is not sufficient alone (§12 has additional pending items); the commit message and §12 update must not inadvertently claim the protocol is LOCKED when other §12 items remain open.

Scope-amendment obligation under §9: adding the --attention-budget flag to shadowbench-runner and changing the calibration script model from stability-maximizer to null-player (if corrected) may constitute a 'deferred to v0.2+' item being pulled into v0.1 — audit the three-tier scope declaration referenced in §9 to confirm this work is in-scope for v0.1 and does not require a dated scope-amendment commit.

shadow-work-nzcy dependency chain: PROTOCOL.md §12 notes the attention-budget line blocks shadow-work-nzcy (DRAFT→LOCKED checklist); confirm that closing shadow-work-5koq and recording the locked value is sufficient to unblock shadow-work-nzcy, or whether shadow-work-nzcy also depends on the noise-floor re-measurement at the locked budget (which is a separate open item).

Commit hash reference in §3: PROTOCOL.md §3 requires a locked scoring-formula commit hash to be set at lock-transition; the attention-budget lock is separate from the scoring-formula lock, but if both happen in the same commit, verify that §3 references that commit hash and not a different one — a stale or wrong hash in §3 would invalidate the scoring-parameter lock.

severity_examples.condition: A replicator running rescore.ipynb from the tarball cannot reproduce the pick decision because the traces were not generated by the protocol-specified agent; the lock is unverifiable and would fail an independent audit under §10's dispute policy
severity_examples.scenario: §7a is updated with the picked value but the calibration tarball is not committed, or the tarball is committed with traces from the wrong model (stability-maximizer instead of null-player)

severity_examples.condition: Other §12 items (ToS decision, pa-reviewer commitment, Amaran probe) are still open; the premature LOCKED status creates a false protocol record and invalidates the lock-transition integrity; any frontier-model run citing this commit as the locked protocol is citing an incomplete document
severity_examples.scenario: The commit that locks §7a also inadvertently sets 'status: LOCKED' in the PROTOCOL.md header

severity_examples.condition: Any future re-calibration (e.g., post-sim-change) will silently use the wrong agent again; the script becomes a reproducibility liability rather than a reproducibility asset
severity_examples.scenario: The calibration script (calibrate-attention-budget.sh) is committed with stability-maximizer still in line 23 after the protocol locks null-baseline as the calibration criterion

success_hints: A single atomic commit updates §7a, §12, and commits the calibration tarball under docs/design/calibration/attention-budget/ — no intermediate state exists where §7a is locked without the tarball.
The PROTOCOL.md status field remains 'DRAFT' after the attention-budget lock; the document header comment notes which §12 items remain open.
The calibration script's inline comment and model flag are updated to null-player so future re-runs match the recorded protocol criterion.
task_context: The brainstorm specifies four deliverables that must land together to close shadow-work-5koq and unblock shadow-work-nzcy. This review checks whether the protocol-document update, tarball artifacts, and dependency chain are handled correctly without premature status changes or incomplete artifact sets.
